Subject: Sizing & timeline for Dedicated cluster — initial scoping

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the final stages of scoping a Dedicated cluster for a priority customer pilot and need a clear picture on procurement lead times and options. High-level ask: we think we'll need ~40 x A100-class nodes (80GB preferred) in us-west. Target start date for pilot is late Q4 (around 2028-11-15), with production ramp in Q1 2029.

Key constraints from our side:
- We need predictable latency (<= 120ms p95 for chat workloads) and at least 2k concurrent sessions during pilot.
- Security requirement: VPC/private deployment; keys managed by our KMS.
- Contract signature target: 2028-07-15 (we're trying to lock pricing by then).

Questions for Redwood:
1) If we commit to Dedicated for the pilot, what are typical OEM lead times we should expect for a full reserved-on-premish fleet (onsite racks or co-lo)?
2) Do you offer a hybrid backstop (cloud reserved instances) while OEM hardware is provisioning? How would pricing and routing work?
3) What documentation do you need to lock a reservation (LOI/PO/contract)?

Would be great to get a short checklist and any ballpark ETAs/quotes so we can align procurement timelines. Happy to hop on a 30m call this week.

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear constraints. Short answers first:

- OEM lead times for A100-class racks are variable but we'd plan for 10–18 weeks once a reservation is placed; longer if specific SKUs are constrained.
- Yes — we routinely pair Dedicated reservations with a cloud backstop. Typically we run a routing policy that prefers Dedicated once healthy, and falls back to reserved cloud capacity (or preemptible where acceptable) for early traffic. Pricing for the backstop is a blended construct we can model for you.
- To trigger an OEM reservation we typically ask for a signed LOI or PO with a non-refundable initial deposit; we can walk through contract terms that align to your sign date.

To make this operational I attached a short capacity checklist and a lightweight template (capacity_template.xlsx) — if you can fill the fields below we can produce: an OEM ETA estimate, a cloud-backstop cost model, and an internal rolling-procurement runbook.

Info we need (short checklist):
- Final node SKU preference (A100-80GB, H100, other).
- Average and peak sequence length, tokens-per-infer request, and target p95 latency.
- Expected ramp (pilot concurrency and production peak).
- Preferred deployment model: co-lo racks vs co-managed on-prem vs cloud-dedicated.
- Contract trigger date (what step triggers reserving hardware).

If you're free Thursday 6/13 I can run through this with Karthik (hardware ops) and Laura (onboarding).

Ben

Ben — quick update and preliminary lane checks. I pinged our contacts at OSK (Nate Hart) and GigaNodes; here's what came back in the initial window: 

- OSK (A100-80GB): lead time 12–16 weeks from PO confirmation for a batch of 40; expedite available for +20% cost and 4–6 week lead time (subject to SKU availability). OSK requires 20% deposit to reserve lane, 50% on ship, 30% on acceptance.
- GigaNodes (A100 family): lead time 14–20 weeks; limited 4-week expedite only for previously allocated inventory customers. Deposit terms similar.

Recommendation: split sourcing 60/40 (OEM / cloud) — lock 24 nodes with an OEM deposit now and cover the rest with reserved cloud instances to meet pilot start date. That reduces exposure to a single vendor and buys time for OEM fulfillment.

I'm attaching the pro-forma I received from OSK (oem_quote_v2.pdf) with lane-breakdown and expedited pricing. I've also sketched the LOI language below that would be sufficient for lane reservation.

Suggested LOI trigger (draft):
- Redwood and Stargaze agree to reserve N nodes (SKU) with OEM partner OSK.
- Stargaze issues LOI specifying count, region, and deposit amount (20% of hardware list).
- OEM acknowledges receipt and places queue hold; deposit credited to final invoice.

I'll follow up with a cloud backstop price estimate once Laura shares her model.

– Karthik
